report_name: 'Zombie Card' Attack Can Revive Expired Visa Cards for Contactless Payments

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: A man-in-the-middle relay, implemented with two NFC-enabled phones, was used to intercept and alter communication between an expired Visa card and a point-of-sale terminal.

attack_patterns.name: Transmitted Data Manipulation
attack_patterns.description: The attack modifies the card's expiration date (Tag-Length-Value tag 5F24) in transit to the payment terminal, allowing an offline transaction to be approved.

vulnerabilities.name: Zombie Card Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in the EMV contactless protocol used by Visa cards that allows an attacker to modify the expiration date in transit during an offline transaction. The attack exploits a discrepancy in how the card communicates its expiration date, specifically by altering the '5F24' tag read by the POS terminal.
affected_products: Visa contactless credit and debit cards

campaigns.name: Zombie Card Attack
campaigns.description: A proof-of-concept attack developed by researchers that allows expired Visa contactless cards to be used for fraudulent payments via a man-in-the-middle relay attack that modifies the card's expiration date.
campaigns.objective: Demonstrate the feasibility of conducting fraudulent transactions with expired contactless cards.

identities.name: Visa
identities.description: The provider of the contactless credit and debit cards affected by the Zombie Card vulnerability.

identities.name: University of Massachusetts Amherst
identities.description: The university where the security researchers who developed and demonstrated the 'Zombie Card' attack are based.

infrastructure.name: Zombie Card MitM Relay Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A man-in-the-middle relay system, implemented using two NFC-enabled Android phones running custom software, to intercept, modify, and forward transaction data from an expired card to a POS terminal.
